claim: Literature value (not computed): at z=0 the OWLS AGN model (van Daalen et al. 2011, arXiv:1104.1174) suppresses power relative to DMO by 1% at k~0.3 h/Mpc, 10% at k~1 h/Mpc and 30% at k~10 h/Mpc. That gives k(1%)~0.3 h/Mpc, S(k=1)~0.90 and S(10)~0.70, with cooling dominant only at k>~70 h/Mpc. On this basis it serves as the strong, fiducial-AGN reference point.

Literature (FLAMINGO, arXiv:2410.17109, not computed): the response gets stronger and its minimum moves to smaller scales as z falls. Lower cluster gas fractions and collimated jets (instead of thermal winds) strengthen the suppression. The strongest FLAMINGO models agree with some WL+external-data analyses but are in strong tension with X-ray cluster gas fractions. The GP emulator is accurate to 1% for k<10 h/Mpc and z<3. No numerical S_min or k_min values were extracted within the budget.

Amon & Efstathiou (arXiv:2206.11794) model the non-linear power as P = P_L + A_mod(P_NL - P_L). With Planck LCDM fixed, a fit to KiDS-1000 cosmic shear needs A_mod ~ 0.69, which is a suppression stronger than recent hydro simulations give. The tension being addressed is KiDS-1000 shear S8 = 0.759+0.024-0.021 and DES Y3 shear S8 = 0.772+0.018-0.017, against Planck S8 = 0.829+-0.012. That is about 9% (2.4-2.7 sigma) low for KiDS and about 7% (2.3-2.6 sigma) low for DES.

Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (arXiv:2305.09827) find that DES Y3 cosmic shear needs a milder non-linear suppression than KiDS-1000 to agree with Planck LCDM. It is still more extreme than recent simulations, and it must extend into the mildly non-linear regime, to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. They name non-standard dark matter as an alternative cause. The DES best-fit A_mod value was not read in the sections examined.

FLAMINGO (McCarthy et al., arXiv:2309.07959) compares its full suite, including extreme feedback variants, with cosmic shear, CMB lensing, tSZ and their cross-spectra. It concludes that baryonic effects are not large enough to remove the S8 tension. Current cosmic shear data are only marginally sensitive to baryon physics. Stronger feedback improves the D3A-cosmology fit to KiDS/DES only slightly, and that preference largely goes away once a lower S8 is adopted. CMB lensing agrees well with Plan

Bigwood et al. (arXiv:2404.06098) fit DES Y3 WL + ACT DR5 kSZ with BCEmu baryonification. They get S8 = 0.823+0.019-0.020, higher than WL alone. The fit prefers a mean feedback scenario more extreme than most hydro simulations. At M500 ~ 1e13 Msun the baryon fraction comes out about 1.4 sigma below HSC-XXL X-ray. At M500 ~ 4e13 Msun, FLAMINGO predicts f_b about 1.5 sigma higher, MillenniumTNG about 3.1 sigma higher and FABLE about 1.4 sigma higher; BAHAMAS agrees best. They also state that model

Literature (BCemu, Giri and Schneider, arXiv:2108.08863, not computed): fitting X-ray group and cluster gas fractions gives a z=0 suppression above the percent level at k=0.1-0.4 h/Mpc (so k(1%) lies at 0.1-0.4 h/Mpc). The maximum suppression is 20-28% (S_min ~0.72-0.80) at k~7 h/Mpc, 68% CL. The OWLS-AGN value of 30% at k=10 h/Mpc sits just beyond the strong edge of this band. The FLAMINGO strongest jet and low-fgas models are stated to be in strong tension with X-ray gas fractions.

The abstracts give three more results. KiDS-1000 lensing x tSZ (arXiv:2109.04458, HMx) prefers strong feedback on its own and finds the amplitude sigma8(Om/0.3)^0.2 about 2 sigma low versus Planck; adding cosmic shear tightens S8 by 40% and gives feedback consistent with hydro simulations. DES Y3 harmonic-space shear (arXiv:2203.07128) finds S8 = 0.793+0.038-0.025 (1.5 sigma below Planck), and extending to k_max = 5 h/Mpc constrains feedback while leaving S8 essentially unchanged. OWLS AGN (van Daalen+2011, arXiv:1104.1174) at z=0: P_hydro/P_DMO falls by 1% at k~0.3, 10% at k~1 and 30% at k~10 h/Mpc; cooling raises power only for k>~70 h/Mpc.

van Daalen+2019 (arXiv:1906.00968, 92 OWLS/cosmo-OWLS/BAHAMAS spectra): the large-scale suppression comes from feedback heating gas and ejecting it to large distances, which is needed to match X-ray groups. An empirical model that uses only the mean baryon fraction in groups predicts the z=0 suppression to within 1% for k<1 h/Mpc, and differences in group baryon fraction explain the disagreement between simulations.

van Loon and van Daalen 2023 (arXiv:2309.06479, cosmo-OWLS/BAHAMAS): AGN feedback ejects matter from inside r500c to r200m and possibly beyond in haloes with M500c>~1e13 Msun/h. For k<~3 h/Mpc, group-sized haloes (1e14+-0.25 Msun/h) dominate the power spectrum; at smaller scales the summed contribution of lower-mass haloes takes over. A lower AGN heating temperature damps the effect at k>~4 h/Mpc for M500c>=1e13.25. A parameter-free model built on halo baryon fractions reaches percent-level accu

Horizon-AGN (Chisari+2018, arXiv:1801.08559) is the weak end of the bracket: suppression at k~10 h/Mpc is <15% at z=0, with an enhancement of a factor of a few at smaller scales from cooling and star formation. Its redshift evolution over z=0-5 is non-monotonic, and the authors conclude its AGN feedback is probably not strong enough.

Elbers+2024 (FLAMINGO, arXiv:2403.12967): baryonic feedback is coupled to cosmology through f_b/c_v^2 ~ f_b/(Omega_m sigma8)^(1/4), which gives an accurate fitting formula for the suppression. Combined baryonic and non-baryonic suppression (neutrinos, decaying DM) is larger than the sum of its parts.

The HACC hydro emulator varies 7 parameters (kappa_w 2-4, e_w 0.2-1.0, M_seed 0.6-2.0 x1e6 Msun, v_kin 0.1-1.2 x1e4 km/s, eps_kin 0.02-1.2 x10, omega_m=Omega_m h^2 0.12-0.155, sigma_8 0.7-0.9). It has no Omega_b or baryon-fraction parameter, so it cannot isolate S(k) as a function of Omega_b/Omega_m (part c is not supported). Pk-ratio is trained at z=0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 (799 k bins). fGas has only 3 M500c bins and is trained at z=0 to 0.9996.
